rootQuestion.question: how does the existing-root durability confirmation (an operational fsync effect that changes no logical bytes) interact with selected read-only surfaces — especially doctor/query/recover — and their exact permission rules?
rootQuestion.answer: there IS a remaining concrete conflict, in three parts; one is resolved in the draft's favour but stated too weakly, two are open
rootQuestion.theFenceIsNotTheBlocker: selected S7's command->lease map places doctor / trust doctor / store status in the 'none (fence only, no project lock)' row and query / recommend / baseline show / policy show|test / candidates / inspect / review brief / repair preview / agent serve reads in SHARED-READ. All of them take the Level-0 fence, so §5's first conjunct is satisfiable by all of them.
rootQuestion.theBarrierIsTheBlocker: selected security-completion.v8 §5.6: the durability primitives' 'costs are paid only at operation boundaries and decisions (§3.3), never by metadata-only commands or doctor'. §3.3's doctor row is 'Durable writes: none' and 'Must not open: any file for writing under the install root'. So doctor / trust doctor / store status are CATEGORICALLY barred by selected law from §5's reconfirmation — they satisfy half the gate and can never satisfy the other half.
rootQuestion.fsyncIsNotItselfA33Violation: an fsync on a directory fd opens no file for writing, and the I-parent is not under the install root; §5.6's cost-scoping sentence is what forbids it, not §3.3's 'must not open' column
rootQuestion.openPart1: query and the whole SHARED-READ set have NO §3.3 class at all (§3.3 defines exactly three: metadata-only, doctor, operation). §5.6 forbids only metadata-only and doctor, so for query the primitives are neither authorized nor forbidden. §5 makes the gate a precondition for producing a binding capability and §7 runs ordinary binding 'under one admitted installation fence', so two readings are equally available and give opposite behaviour — see B-1(b).
rootQuestion.openPart2: doctor's selected parity fields are report-produced, outcome, defects-found, defects, offline-window, termination-class — there is NO capability-availability or availability field, while query has availability (/queryResponse/context/availability) and default/analyze/fit/audit have capability-availability. The one new failure mode §4 introduces (visible complete, durability unconfirmed) therefore has no declared rendering channel on the only selected diagnostic surface, while §6 sends a post-creator-death process to run a gate doctor may not run — see B-1(c).
rootQuestion.precedentToCite: unselected host-foundation-completion.v2 §1 already contains the right sentence: 'Read-only commands report absence without creating it.'

requiredFindings.finding: The read-only surface interaction is left as an open conditional whose condition selected law has already settled, and two parts of it are genuinely undecided. Resolving them at implementation time would silently let read-only surfaces pay durability costs selected §5.6 does not authorize.
requiredFindings.required: (a) Replace 'If an execution surface forbids even durability confirmation…' with a determination citing security-completion.v8 §5.6 and naming doctor / trust doctor / store status as permanently provisional for installation durability, noting that the fence is not the blocker. (b) Decide whether §7's ordinary binding under the fence requires §5's gate for the SHARED-READ surfaces, which have no §3.3 class: either state a read-only binding path that does not require the gate, or accept they are provisional and reconcile that with query's selected goldens (query-latest-empty, query-completeness-unmet) and parity fields. (c) Say where a visible-complete-durability-unconfirmed installation is reported on doctor; if it needs a parity field, name that as a required change to a selected inventory.

requiredFindings.finding: At first creation, selected S3.1's three backup-custody remedies collapse to one, and §392 never says so. --ephemeral is excluded by §1a; the already-admitted host storage-policy record has no home because §1b declines the older proposal's mutable settings files and §2's complete initial tree contains none; only --allow-backup-custody survives. §1b additionally removes the inventory golden's prose remedy 'select another admitted root' by forbidding every override. On a BACKED_UP macOS home in CI (which never prompts), installation creation therefore requires --allow-backup-custody on the very first invocation.
requiredFindings.required: State this consequence, and say whether a first-creation storage policy is intended to become possible later. §1a step 5's 'still follows the existing storage policy' currently implies a route that structurally cannot exist yet.
requiredFindings.note: UNKNOWN backup status still admits with a mandatory disclosure, so this bites only on positive BACKED_UP

requiredFindings.finding: §6's disposition table has no row for 'I absent, invocation not eligible to create'. Five selected commands carry firstSourceWrite:true but authority:none — import, baseline-upgrade, repair-apply, test-run, native-prepare — and S7 places them in APPEND-WRITE or EXCLUSIVE. §1a correctly refuses them the creator role and §1 says they 'cannot enter' it, but nothing says what they return on a fresh machine.
requiredFindings.required: Add the row and state the exact result. Without it, five selected commands have undefined behaviour on a fresh machine and the natural wrong answers (run ephemerally, or create I anyway) are both things this owner exists to prevent.

requiredFindings.finding: Identity §5 requires reporting retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture; it does NOT require the disclosure to identify the storage root. §1a step 1 adds that content and step 5 makes it load-bearing ('The initial storage-root disclosure must match this actual account-derived target'), inside a step described as building on identity §5.

requiredFindings.finding: §2 says the new law is 'their required ordering, owner retention and scoped receipts, not a new flush vocabulary'. True of the primitive, but §5.6's Boundaries list (witness write, evalHighWater write, journal append, quarantine marker, SC-TRUST high-water copy, lifecycle publication, selection commit) does not include the H barrier, the per-ancestor directory+parent barriers, the stage-internal barriers, the post-rename I-parent barrier, or §5's existing-root reconfirmation.

requiredFindings.finding: §9's implementation-obligation list omits two distinct load-bearing items the body identifies: a pre-installation platform evidence producer that does not require a fence (§1a step 4), and a qualified profile premise that the account-home base remains durably reachable (§3). I verified the first against the product: native_platform.rs:27 is `pub(super) struct NativePlatformEvidence<'f> { fence: &'f SuppliedInstallationFence, … }`.
requiredFindings.required: Enumerate both in §9, which is the list that will be actioned.
